title_zh: MacroVoices #553 Brent Johnson（Santiago Capital）：《Disparate Housewives》——美联储与财政部的“联姻”
subtitle_zh: Brent Johnson 解析美元突破、黄金重估与美联储和财政部联手背后的宏观博弈
summary_zh: 本期 MacroVoices 由 Eric Townsend 与 Patrick Ceresna 对话 Santiago Capital 创始人 Brent Johnson。在多数同行看空美元之际，Johnson 是唯一唱多美元指数（DXY）的人，而 DXY 周三收于 1.02 上方印证了他的判断。他解释美元突破的几点驱动：市场要求更高利率、Warsh 执掌美联储后为建立公信力反而加息；「你还能去哪儿」——欧洲增长乏力、有政治联盟却无财政联盟，日本问题缠身，中国是封闭市场；以及 AI 交易或许意味着增长、令持有债券需要更高回报。节目重点拆解他付费报告《Disparate Housewives》的执行摘要，以「联姻」类比美联储与财政部的协作，并指出过去五到十年出现的新技术——稳定币（stablecoins）——正把筹码重新交回财政部手里，因为稳定币无需银行体系即可分发债券、筹集现金与完成支付。Johnson 还谈到「重新货币化黄金」、美元奶昔理论（dollar milkshake theory）、当前更像对华冷战开端而非其他常被类比的时代，以及 AI 在达到「逃逸速度」（escape velocity）前可能带来的颠簸。结尾 Trading Desk 聚焦天然气创纪录空头持仓与潜在逼空（squeeze）风险。

turns.en: I've been doing this for 26 years now, and for 25 of the 26 years, I've been hearing that the Fed is out of bullets. And my point to people is that they have a lot more bullets than you can possibly imagine.
turns.zh: 我做这行已经26年了，其中25年里我一直听人说美联储没子弹了。我想告诉大家的是，他们的子弹比你所能想象的要多得多。

turns.en: That was Santiago Capital founder Brent Johnson. I'm Eric Townsend, and this is Macrovoices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional finance and sophisticated private investors.
turns.zh: 刚才那段是 Santiago Capital 创始人 Brent Johnson。我是 Eric Townsend，这里是 MacroVoices，一档面向专业金融人士和成熟个人投资者的免费周更播客。

turns.en: Episode 553 was produced on October 8th, 2026. Brent Johnson has been the lone voice calling for a higher dollar index while most of his peers were dollar bears.
turns.zh: 第553期节目制作于2026年10月8日。在大多数同行都看空美元的时候，Brent Johnson 一直是唯一那个唱多美元指数的人。

turns.en: With the Dixie closing above 1.02 on Wednesday afternoon, we were long overdue to get Brent back on the program. And Brent just released a paywalled research report titled Disparate Housewives, an analogy to the apparent marriage of the Fed and Treasury Department.
turns.zh: 随着美元指数（DXY）周三下午收于1.02上方，我们早该把 Brent 请回节目了。而且 Brent 刚发布了一份付费研究报告，标题叫《Disparate Housewives》，用来类比美联储和财政部之间那场显而易见的“联姻”。

turns.en: That is behind a paywall, but we were able to persuade Brent to let us share at least the executive summary with you, and that's linked in your research roundup email.
turns.zh: 那份报告在付费墙后面，但我们说服了 Brent，至少让他同意把执行摘要分享给大家，链接就在你的 research roundup 邮件里。

turns.en: We'll discuss all of that, plus gold, the formative Cold War with China, and much more in this week's feature interview. And I'm Patrick Ceresna.
turns.zh: 我们会聊所有这些，还有黄金、正在成形的对华冷战等等，都在本周的重点访谈里。我是 Patrick Ceresna。

turns.en: Let's dive into this interview. Brent prepared a slide deck to accompany this week's interview, and I strongly encourage you to download it.
turns.zh: 让我们进入这期访谈。Brent 为本周的访谈准备了一套幻灯片，我强烈建议你下载。

turns.en: Registered users will find it in your research roundup email, or you can just go to our homepage, macrovoices.com. Look for the red button above Brent's picture that says looking for the downloads.
turns.zh: 注册用户可以在 research roundup 邮件里找到它，或者直接去我们主页 macrovoices.com，找 Brent 照片上方那个写着 looking for the downloads 的红色按钮。

turns.en: And it's great to get you back on. I want to start with the reason I brought you back on, which is boy, all of us smart guys don't listen to that crazy nutcase Brent Johnson.
turns.zh: 很高兴又能请你来。我想先说说我为什么把你请回来，就是——哎呀，我们这帮聪明人都不听 Brent Johnson 这个疯子的话。

turns.en: We know the dollar index can't possibly break out above 100 here. Oops, just did. You're the man who called it. So what's going on here? Why is the dollar breaking out now?
turns.zh: 我们都知道美元指数不可能在这儿突破100。哎哟，刚突破了。你就是那个说中了的人。那到底怎么回事？美元为什么现在突破？

turns.en: For me, it was an unexpected move, although I think you've been anticipating it. Yeah. Well, we're at a pretty interesting time right now. I think over the summer, a lot of people were expecting now that we've got to wash and power at the Fed, and they're going to coordinate perfectly with Trump, and they're just going to cut rates, and the dollar is going to fall, and that's kind of it.
turns.zh: 对我来说这是个意外的走势，不过我想你一直在等着它出现。是的。嗯，我们现在正处在一个相当有意思的时点。我觉得整个夏天很多人都以为，既然现在 Warsh 已经执掌了美联储，他们会跟 Trump 完美配合，只会降息，美元会下跌，就这样了。

turns.en: It just once again shows you just never know with markets, right? There is no certainty. And I think to a certain extent, markets are demanding higher rates.
turns.zh: 这再一次说明，市场永远捉摸不定，对吧？没有什么是确定的。而且我觉得在某种程度上，市场正在要求更高的利率。

turns.en: And in order to establish at least some credibility early on, wash went the other way and has raised rates. Raising rates is a big part of it, but I think there's other parts of it as well.
turns.zh: 而为了在一开始就建立起哪怕一点点公信力，Warsh 反其道而行，加息了。加息是其中很重要的一部分，但我觉得还有其他因素。

turns.en: I think there's kind of three other parts. Number one is where else are you going to go, right? Do you really want to go to Europe that has a war raging on its border, very little economic growth, and a political union without a fiscal union?
turns.zh: 我觉得大概还有另外三点。第一是，你还能去哪儿，对吧？你真的想去欧洲吗？那儿边界上战火正酣，经济增长乏善可陈，还是个有政治联盟却没有财政联盟的地方。

turns.en: That doesn't seem too attractive to me. Japan still has a number of problems. I don't see a lot of global capital flowing to Japan, maybe a little bit.
turns.zh: 这在我看来没什么吸引力。日本仍然有一堆问题。我看不到大量全球资本流向日本，也许会有一点。

turns.en: But again, that's not necessarily a safe haven. China's kind of got a closed market. It's possible to get in there, but not in a big way. And do you really want to go there when there's a trade war going on between the United States and China?
turns.zh: 但那也未必是避险港湾。中国算是个封闭市场，进得去，但没法大规模进。而且在中美贸易战正打得火热的时候，你真的想去那儿吗？

turns.en: And so in some ways, the world still needs dollars to operate. The world still sells things to the United States in dollars. Therefore they earn dollars, therefore they have borrowed in dollars, and in order to match liabilities to expenses or revenues and not have to be a currency trader, they store their money in dollars.
turns.zh: 所以在某些方面，世界运转仍然需要美元。世界仍然用美元向美国卖东西，因此他们赚美元，因此他们借的是美元，而为了让负债和支出或收入相匹配、又不必去当个外汇交易员，他们就把钱存成美元。

turns.en: And so that creates a bid for dollars. The other part of it that I think is a little bit less appreciated, and this is not necessarily my base case, but I can't rule it out, is that rates I think are also higher because to a certain extent this AI ecosystem is perhaps saying maybe we're not going to go into this great reset, maybe we're not going to have this great depression, maybe we're actually
turns.zh: 这就形成了对美元的买盘。另一部分我觉得没那么被充分理解——这不一定是我的基准情形，但我无法排除——就是利率之所以更高，某种程度上是因为这个 AI 生态系统也许在说，也许我们不会进入这场大重置（great reset），也许我们不会迎来大萧条，也许我们其实正

turns.en: coming into something that's going to provide some growth, and perhaps they can kick this down the road further than we think. And because of the growth associated with the AI trade, we need to get paid more to sit in bonds, et cetera, et cetera.
turns.zh: 步入某种能带来一些增长的东西，也许他们能把这个问题往后拖得比我们想的更久。而由于 AI 交易带来的增长，我们持有债券就需要拿到更多回报，等等等等。

turns.en: So I think there's that part of it. And I think all of that feeds into owning the dollar. Because again, to take advantage of any of those three different things I've talked about so far, you first need to have dollars.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得有这一层因素。而且我认为所有这些最终都指向持有美元。因为同样地，要利用我目前谈到的这三件不同的事情中的任何一件，你首先都得有美元。

turns.en: Now what you do with those dollars, whether you buy a T-bill, whether you buy some U.S. real estate, whether you buy stocks, or maybe you just sit in cash, that's another decision to make.
turns.zh: 至于你拿这些美元去做什么——是买国库券（T-bill），是买点美国房地产，是买股票，还是干脆持币观望——那是另一个要做的决定。

turns.en: But the first decision to be made is to buy dollars. Now I'm trying to think back to the last time we spoke, I thought at one point your dollar milkshake theory, and I should mention that for any new listeners not familiar with Brent's work, definitely Google Brent Johnson dollar milkshake or better yet put those search terms into the search box at Macrovoices.com, listen to some of Brent's prior interviews
turns.zh: 但要做的第一个决定就是买美元。现在我想回想一下我们上次聊的时候，我记得有一阵子你的美元奶昔理论（dollar milkshake theory）——我得提一句，任何还不熟悉 Brent 工作的新听众，一定要去 Google 搜 Brent Johnson dollar milkshake，或者更好，把这些搜索词输进 Macrovoices.com 的搜索框，听听 Brent 之前那些

turns.en: about that. I think at one point you were kind of expecting a higher than the high we had a couple of years ago, at 1.16 or whatever it was on the dollar index.
turns.zh: 相关的访谈。我记得有一阵子你预期会比我们几年前那个高点还要高，就是美元指数1.16左右那个高点。

turns.en: And I thought you had revised that later to say maybe not, maybe that was the high. What's your outlook now? Can we go even higher on the dollar?
turns.zh: 我以为你后来修正了看法，说也许不会，也许那就是高点了。你现在怎么看？美元还能涨得更高吗？

turns.en: I think we can. So I think we're at a really interesting point right now. If you look at the charts on the dollar and you look at kind of the momentum and the stochastics and the positioning, all of this kind of stuff, it wouldn't surprise me if the dollar gets a short-term pullback because the dollar is very high, the momentum is very high.
turns.zh: 我觉得能。所以我们现在正处在一个非常有意思的点上。如果你看美元的图表，看动能、随机指标（stochastics）和持仓这些东西，美元出现短期回调我一点都不意外，因为美元已经涨得很高，动能也很强。

turns.en: The narrative around the dollar now is it's no longer a shock. People have already been surprised, but with the euro, the euros kind of fallen dramatically.
turns.zh: 现在围绕美元的叙事是，它已经不再令人震惊了。人们已经被惊到过一轮了。而欧元这边，欧元已经大幅下跌。

turns.en: Positioning come down, sentiment is gone, momentum is gone in the euro, and kind of the same with gold. Gold's kind of at a pretty interesting place here.
turns.zh: 持仓降下来了，情绪没了，欧元的动能也没了，黄金也差不多是同样的情况。黄金现在处在一个相当有意思的位置。

turns.en: The momentum on gold has gone away, the narrative on gold has gone away, and it just had a golden cross actually where the 50-day moving average came up through the 100-day moving average.
turns.zh: 黄金的动能已经消退，围绕黄金的叙事也消退了，而且它刚刚走了个黄金交叉（golden cross），50日均线上穿了100日均线。

turns.en: So in the very short term, I think it's very possible we get a short-term pullback in the dollar and perhaps a bounce in the euro and gold. But more of the longer term, I still think that we can go back to much higher levels on the dollar.
turns.zh: 所以在极短期内，我觉得美元很可能出现短期回调，欧元和黄金也许会反弹。但把时间拉长一点，我仍然认为美元能重新回到高得多的水平。

turns.en: What I would say, what I just said about the dollar pulling back, if the dollar does not pull back here and it continues to go higher, kind of heaven helped the world because it's already kind of in a precarious place and if the dollar goes much higher, it's going to start to break some things.
turns.zh: 我要说的是，关于我刚才讲的美元回调，如果美元在这里不回调、反而继续走高，那真是老天爷帮帮这世界了，因为它已经处在一个相当危险的境地，如果美元再涨得多一些，就会开始搞坏一些东西。

turns.en: Now, my original prediction on the dollar going back to the first time I gave it at your conference back in 2019 was I thought we had a particular set of circumstances ahead of us that could see the dollar as part of a global sovereign debt crisis return to its all-time highs.
turns.zh: 说到我最初对美元的预测——回到我第一次提出它的时候，是在2019年你们的会议上——我当时认为，我们面前有着一组特定的情势，可能让美元作为一场全球主权债务危机的一部分，重新回到它的历史高点。

turns.en: And we got pretty close in 2020 and we got close again in 2022. But ultimately, it didn't happen. The powers that be were able to kick the can down the road.
turns.zh: 2020年我们离得很近，2022年又接近了一次。但最终它没有发生。当权者成功地把问题往后拖了。

turns.en: And there's been a few things that have happened since that believes me to believe that potentially they can kick the can down the road even further than I initially thought.
turns.zh: 而此后发生的一些事情让我相信，他们也许能把这个问题往后拖得比我最初设想的更久。

turns.en: And so I'm not necessarily predicting a super spike in the dollar in the short term. But if we do get to this end game scenario, if we do get to this sovereign debt crisis level, I think it's more likely that the dollar shoots higher than the dollar shoots lower.
turns.zh: 所以我并不一定在预测短期内美元会剧烈飙升。但如果我们真的走到那个终局情形，真的到了主权债务危机那个级别，我认为美元向上飙升比向下暴跌的可能性更大。

turns.en: So while the milkshake as a prediction event of a global sovereign debt crisis was wrong, the direction that I said the assets would travel as a result of that sovereign debt crisis has been correct.
turns.zh: 所以，尽管奶昔理论作为对一场全球主权债务危机的预测是错的，但我当时说的、那场主权债务危机会导致各类资产走向的方向，却是对的。

turns.en: So the framework has still been useful to me when allocating capital. Now, you mentioned gold. Let's go a little deeper there because what's fascinated me on this particular dollar move is, OK, gold is softening here, but it's not crashing to new lows the way it was a few months ago.
turns.zh: 所以这个框架在我配置资本时仍然有用。你提到了黄金。我们往深里聊聊，因为这轮美元走势让我着迷的地方在于，好，黄金在这儿走软，但它并没有像几个月前那样崩到新低。

turns.en: Is the bottom in already? I mean, let's suppose that we are going to see a move back to 110 on the Dixie. Does gold crash to below 4,000 or is it already found a bottom?
turns.zh: 底部已经到了吗？我是说，假设我们真会看到美元指数（DXY）回到110。黄金会跌破4000吗，还是它已经找到底部了？

turns.en: If we go to 110 on the dollar index, I think gold probably goes lower, maybe to the $3,700 range. It's already, I think, around 4,100. It kind of made a low over the summer.
turns.zh: 如果美元指数到110，我觉得黄金大概率会走低，也许到3700美元那个区间。它现在我想大概在4100左右，整个夏天算是走了个低点。

turns.en: It had a really good run, peaked its head above the 200-day moving average and then has rolled back over. I think it's at a really interesting point right here because it's kind of at a longer turn, not long, long term, but it's kind of at a support area.
turns.zh: 它有过一波很好的涨势，冒头站上200日均线，然后又回落下来。我觉得它现在就处在一个很有意思的点上，因为它算是到了一个较长的转折位——不是很长很长期的，但算是到了一个支撑区。

turns.en: And I think if it breaks that support, then it could fall another 10%. But listen, I'll tell you, I just yesterday I bought some gold for a client.
turns.zh: 我觉得如果它跌破那个支撑，就可能再跌10%。不过听着，我跟你说，就在昨天我还为一个客户买了一些黄金。

turns.en: And so I think this is probably the area to start nibbling on it. I think because of where we're at with the dollar, because of where we're at with the euro, because where we're at with gold and the fact that it just made this a golden cross, I actually think the gold's going to make a fairly big move in the next few weeks.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这里大概就是开始一点点建仓的区域了。我认为，鉴于美元现在的位置、欧元现在的位置、黄金现在的位置，加上它刚走了这个黄金交叉，我实际上觉得黄金在未来几周会有一波相当大的行情。

turns.en: I think it probably goes higher. But if I'm wrong and it goes lower, I would probably be a buyer of that low. But I'll just have to wait and see.
turns.zh: 我觉得它大概率会往上走。但如果我错了、它往下走，那我大概会在那个低点买入。不过这只能走着瞧。

turns.en: I want to move on now to a piece that you wrote recently, which is behind your paywall, but we were lucky enough to get permission from you to publish an executive summary of it.
turns.zh: 我现在想转到你最近写的一篇文章，它在你的付费墙后面，但我们很走运，拿到了你的许可来发表它的执行摘要。

turns.en: Registered users will find that linked in your research roundup email. The piece is called Disparate Housewives, and the metaphor here is Treasury Secretary Scott Besant and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh are kind of like desperate housewives, although I'm not sure if the metaphor might better be that they formed a cult in order to change monetary policy.
turns.zh: 注册用户会在 research roundup 邮件里找到链接。这篇文章叫《Disparate Housewives》，这里的隐喻是：财政部长 Scott Bessent 和美联储主席 Kevin Warsh 有点像“绝望主妇”（desperate housewives），尽管我不确定这个隐喻是不是更该说成，他们组成了一个邪教来改变货币政策。

turns.en: But it seems like they're up to something. They've got big plans, and it's not just to follow in the footsteps of Janet Yellen and Ben Bernanke and so forth.
turns.zh: 但看起来他们正在谋划些什么。他们有大计划，而且不只是要沿着 Janet Yellen 和 Ben Bernanke 等人的老路走。

turns.en: Tell us what the piece is about, and as much as you're willing to disclose, I know it is one of your premium pieces that's behind the paywall.
turns.zh: 跟我们讲讲这篇文章讲的是什么，以及你愿意披露多少——我知道这是你付费墙后面的高端内容之一。

turns.en: Yeah. So I think this is kind of really important to understand, because I think the times are dictating this. And what I wanted to lay out, first I wanted people to understand that in many ways, the power of the United States has been built on the separation of powers and the fact that there was three different branches, and none of them answered to the others, and by dividing this power, it provided a certain level of credibility and structural certainty.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得这一点真的很重要，得理解，因为我认为是时势在推动这件事。我想阐述的是，首先我想让大家明白，在很多方面，美国的实力是建立在三权分立之上的，建立在有三个互不隶属的分支之上，而通过分割这份权力，它提供了某种程度的公信力和结构性确定性。

turns.en: And as part of that, having an independent central bank was part of that. And the Fed and the Treasury have worked together in the past, but they have also been very much at odds in the past.
turns.zh: 而作为其中一部分，拥有一个独立的央行也是这套体系的一部分。美联储和财政部过去曾合作过，但它们过去也曾非常对立。

turns.en: And we've always felt that this idea of Fed independence was the wrong term. We do not think the Fed is independent. We think they have autonomy, but we think that is different than independence.
turns.zh: 而我们一直觉得，“美联储独立”这个说法是个错误的词。我们不认为美联储是独立的。我们认为它有自主权（autonomy），但我们觉得这和“独立”是两回事。

turns.en: If they were fully independent, they wouldn't have to march up to the Capitol two times a year and testify before Congress. If they were fully independent, they wouldn't have needed a charter from Congress making their creation in the world.
turns.zh: 如果它真的完全独立，它就不必每年两次跑到国会山去、在国会面前作证。如果它真的完全独立，它当初就不需要国会颁布一份特许状来让它问世。

turns.en: And so we feel like these times in the past where the Fed and the sovereign or the Fed and the Treasury or the executive branch, however you want to define that, whenever they've come into conflict, and the Fed actually has a pretty good track record in those conflicts, we think that the Fed kind of won because the sovereign didn't push it too hard.
turns.zh: 所以我们觉得，过去每当美联储与主权方、或美联储与财政部、或行政部门——随你怎么界定——发生冲突时，而美联储在这些冲突中其实有着相当不错的战绩，我们认为美联储算是占了上风，因为主权方并没有把它逼得太狠。

turns.en: They just said, okay, you know what, it's not worth it to fight this. But we think that the place that the earth, the world, the market, the global community, however you want to define that, the direction we are heading is into another great power competition.
turns.zh: 他们只是说，好吧，你知道吗，为这个吵架不值得。但我们认为，这个世界、这个市场、这个全球共同体——随你怎么界定——我们所处的这个地球，正在走向的方向，是另一场大国竞争。

turns.en: If you want to call that the great game, if you want to call it geopolitical 3D chess, whatever your terminology for this, we feel like that's where the world is heading.
turns.zh: 如果你想把它叫作“大博弈”（the Great Game），如果你想叫它地缘政治的三维棋局，随你用什么术语，我们觉得世界正在朝那个方向走。

turns.en: And we feel like this great game, this big power competition, is to a certain extent going to demand that the sovereign have full power. And to have full power, you're going to need a united street.
turns.zh: 我们觉得，这场大博弈、这场大国竞争，在某种程度上会要求主权方拥有完整的权力。而要拥有完整的权力，你就需要让“这条街”团结起来（指财政部与美联储步调一致）。

turns.en: And this was the desperate housewives analogy. You know, in many times in the past, the State Department may be moving one way, the monetary policy may be saying something else.
turns.zh: 这就是那个“绝望主妇”的类比。你知道，过去很多时候，国务院可能往一个方向走，货币政策可能在说另一回事。

turns.en: The Treasury might have other goals along with the President, and they weren't necessarily all working together. And as part of Trump kind of reorganizing the rules-based order, and in many ways tearing down the rules-based order and moving towards an America-first strategy, we think the Fed and the Treasury working closer together is going to be one of those, the outcomes of that.
turns.zh: 财政部可能和总统一道有着别的目标，他们未必都在协同行动。而随着 Trump 某种程度上在重组基于规则的秩序（rules-based order）、在很多方面拆解这套秩序并转向“美国优先”（America First）战略，我们认为美联储和财政部更紧密地协作，将会是这其中的一个结果。

turns.en: And I know I'm rambling here, but I want to make this point because I think it's important to understand. I think there's a misperception that the Fed and the Treasury have always worked together or has always worked kind of hand in glove.
turns.zh: 我知道我在这儿有点絮叨，但我想讲清楚这一点，因为我觉得理解它很重要。我认为存在一种误解，觉得美联储和财政部一直在合作、或者一直配合得天衣无缝。

turns.en: But I want to just point out a few different times where that hasn't been the case. There was a big thing called the Fed Treasury Accord back in the 50s, where this became very public and their differences became very volatile.
turns.zh: 但我只想指出几个并非如此的不同时期。上世纪50年代有件大事叫《美联储-财政部协议》（Fed-Treasury Accord），当时双方的分歧变得非常公开、非常激烈。

turns.en: And they came to the Treasury Accord, which said they're each stay in their same lanes. But that doesn't mean they always worked counter to each other, either.
turns.zh: 他们达成了那份财政部协议，规定各自待在自己的赛道里。但这也不意味着他们总是彼此对着干。

turns.en: Of course, sometimes they worked together. But even in recent times, the most recent example I can think of is in 2022 when Powell was raising rates to slow inflation.
turns.zh: 当然，有时候他们也合作。但即便在近些年，我能想到的最近一个例子是2022年，当时 Powell 在加息以抑制通胀。

turns.en: And at the same time, Janet Yellen was drawing down the TGA in the reverse repo and sending liquidity back into the market. That was not working hand in glove.
turns.zh: 而与此同时，Janet Yellen 却在抽减财政部一般账户（TGA）和逆回购（reverse repo），把流动性重新注入市场。那可不是什么协同一致。

turns.en: That was at odds with each other. And what I think is really interesting in the last month is, well, actually, let's say the last 18 months, since Besant has become Treasury Secretary, he has started to wade into policies that would traditionally be considered monetary policy, whether it's Treasury buybacks or whether it's swap lines.
turns.zh: 那是彼此对立。而我觉得过去一个月里非常有趣的一点是——好吧，其实应该说过去18个月，自从 Bessent 出任财政部长以来，他开始介入一些传统上会被视为货币政策的领域，无论是国债回购（Treasury buybacks）还是货币互换额度（swap lines）。

turns.en: Traditionally, that's the area of the Fed. But instead of just staying in his lane, Besant has waded in there quite confidently. And then last month, at the same interview when he started talking about why they were increasing their Treasury buybacks, and he made the comment that I am the house now.
turns.zh: 传统上那是美联储的地盘。但 Bessent 没有只待在自己的赛道里，而是相当自信地插了进去。然后上个月，在同一次访谈里，当他开始谈他们为什么要加大国债回购力度时，他说了一句“我现在就是庄家”（I am the house now）。

turns.en: And that got all the attention. What he said second to that is, I think, more important. When somebody asked him, how did he think that the new Fed share would react to that when he was more of a let the market determine the rate type of a guy, Besant said, we will work together.
turns.zh: 那句话抢走了所有关注。但我觉得他紧接着说的第二句更重要。当有人问他，考虑到新任美联储主席更像是个“让市场来决定利率”类型的人，他觉得对方会作何反应时，Bessent 说，我们会合作。

turns.en: In other words, he didn't say, we're each going to stay in our same lane. He didn't say, you know, they're independent than they can do what they want.
turns.zh: 换句话说，他没有说“我们各自待在自己的赛道里”。他没有说“你知道，他们是独立的，他们想干什么就干什么”。

turns.en: He very clearly said, we're going to work together. And so I think that is where we're headed. Now, whether this is a mutual marriage, whether a shotgun is involved, whether it's public or whether it's private, I think that's yet to be determined, but I think that's where we're headed.
turns.zh: 他非常明确地说，我们会合作。所以我觉得那就是我们要走的方向。至于这是一场两情相悦的婚姻、还是被枪逼着成的婚，是公开的还是私下的，我觉得还有待观察，但我认为那就是我们的方向。

turns.en: And I think that has dramatic consequences for both domestic and world markets going forward. Well, I couldn't agree more on that point. And I would even strengthen it to say, you know, Scott Besant is not only expanding the scope of treasury beyond its traditional meaning, but to my thinking, he's really starting to participate in what I think are wartime policy decisions.
turns.zh: 而且我认为，这无论对国内还是对全球市场，往后都会有剧烈影响。这一点我再同意不过了。我甚至还想强化一下：你知道，Scott Bessent 不只是在把财政部的职责范围扩展到其传统含义之外，在我看来，他其实开始参与到我认为是战时的政策决策中去了。

turns.en: I mean, he's at least consulting, if not actively engaged in helping the Trump administration to design economic sanctions against Iran and so forth.
turns.zh: 我是说，他至少是在咨询、如果不是积极参与的话，帮助 Trump 政府设计对伊朗等等的经济制裁。

turns.en: And whether that's good or bad is a political call that I'll leave to our listeners to make for themselves, but it's definitely different from the way things used to work.
turns.zh: 而这是好是坏，是个政治判断，我就留给我们的听众自己去下结论了，但这确实和过去事情的运作方式不一样。

turns.en: I want to take that a step further though, because one option that they might pursue as we see clearly a trend toward a more liberal interpretation of what staying in their lane means or maybe it's a willingness to cross into another lane, you've described an opportunity where all of the United States sovereign gold holdings are still for a whole bunch of historical reasons marked at a valuation of $42 an ounce when of course it's really a hundred times
turns.zh: 不过我想再往前推一步，因为有一个他们可能会采取的选择——我们清楚地看到一种趋势，就是对“待在自己赛道里”的含义做了更宽松的解读，或者说是一种愿意跨进别人赛道的意愿——你描述过这么一个机会：美国全部的主权黄金储备，出于一大堆历史原因，至今仍按每盎司42美元的估值入账，而它实际上值大约一百倍

turns.en: more that actually slightly less than that. As I look at the gold tape this morning, we're actually dipped below $4,100 a few hours ago before recording this session, but we're at approximately a hundredth of the real value.
turns.zh: 还多，其实稍微少一点。今早我看黄金行情的时候，就在我们录这期节目几个小时之前，它其实一度跌破了4100美元，但我们大致仍处在真实价值的百分之一这个水平。

turns.en: You've said that's all money that could be raised in an afternoon by remarking the gold to market. I think a lot of our listeners would be quick to say, wait a minute, that's nonsense.
turns.zh: 你说过，只要把黄金按市价重新计价，那全都是能在一个下午之内筹到的钱。我想我们很多听众会脱口而出：等等，这是胡说八道。

turns.en: When you have an asset that's marked below market, that's an unrealized gain, you mark it to market. It doesn't raise any money, it just corrects the number that's on your balance sheet to make it realistic.
turns.zh: 当你有一项按低于市价入账的资产时，那是一笔未实现收益，你把它按市价重估，它并不会筹到任何钱，它只是把你资产负债表上的数字修正得更真实而已。

turns.en: It doesn't raise anything, but I think you do make actually a very good point that the accounting rules for the government are different than they are for private investors.
turns.zh: 它筹不到任何东西，但我觉得你确实提出了一个非常好的点，就是政府的会计规则和私人投资者的不一样。

turns.en: So how do you actually raise money in an afternoon by marking the government's gold to market? So this is where I think it gets really interesting, and I think this is the part where the marriage between the Fed and Treasury is really important, or at least if they're not married at least getting along and are able to stay in the same room.
turns.zh: 那么，你究竟是怎么做到、通过把政府的黄金按市价重估，就在一个下午筹到钱的？这就是我觉得真正有意思的地方了，我认为这正是美联储和财政部之间的“联姻”至关重要的部分，或者说，就算他们没结婚，至少也得和睦相处、能待在同一个房间里。

turns.en: Some husbands and wives are not able to stay in the same room with each other, and they would prefer to be as far away from each other as possible.
turns.zh: 有些丈夫和妻子是没法待在同一个房间里的，他们宁愿彼此离得越远越好。

turns.en: But the point I want to make is the government, the US government, arguably the biggest and strongest government in the history of the world does not have its own bank.
turns.zh: 但我想讲的点是，政府——美国政府，可以说是世界历史上最大、最强的政府——却没有自己的银行。

turns.en: The Treasury, or I'm sorry, the Fed is the Treasury's bank. And if the Treasury is working with a bank and that bank is independent, that bank doesn't have to do the sovereign says to do, or what the customer says to do.
turns.zh: 财政部，哦不对，美联储是财政部的银行。而如果财政部合作的这家银行是独立的，那这家银行就不必去做主权方叫它做的事、或者客户叫它做的事。

turns.en: If it's truly independent, it would have the ability to say, no, we're not doing that. Now this is why I say if it came to this, the sovereign would change their tune, and this could all change in a weekend.
turns.zh: 如果它是真正独立的，它就有能力说“不，这个我们不干”。这就是为什么我说，如果真到了这一步，主权方会改变腔调，而这一切可能在一个周末之内就变天。

turns.en: But going to your question is the way that they could have this windfall show up in the Treasury's account is they could tell them that the gold certificates that are on file booking the gold at $42 per ounce, if they were to take that to current market prices of $4,100, when they do that, they mark up the Fed then marks up those gold certificates and they credit to keep the balance sheet balanced, they credit the Treasury's account
turns.zh: 但回到你的问题——他们能让这笔意外之财出现在财政部账户里的方式，是可以告诉他们：那些存档在册、把黄金按每盎司42美元入账的黄金证书（gold certificates），如果把它们按当前市价4100美元重估，那么在他们这么做的时候，美联储就会把这些黄金证书上调，然后为了让资产负债表保持平衡，他们会贷记财政部的账户

turns.en: with that trillion dollars. And that can be done in an afternoon, but it requires the Treasury to say to do it, but then it also requires to Fed to say, okay.
turns.zh: 贷记那一万亿美元。这在一个下午就能办到，但它需要财政部开口叫它做，同时还需要美联储说“好”。

turns.en: And so if you had a Fed and a Treasury that were at odds, and the President said to the Treasury Secretary, we're going to revalue gold higher.
turns.zh: 所以，如果你有一个彼此对立的美联储和财政部，而总统对财政部长说，我们要把黄金往上重估。

turns.en: And the Fed said that's not a policy that we think is appropriate this time. And they had disagreed to accept those higher rated gold certificates, they wouldn't theoretically they would not have to credit that account.
turns.zh: 而美联储说，这不是我们认为此时合适的政策，他们不同意接受那些按更高估值计的黄金证书，那么理论上他们就不必贷记那个账户。

turns.en: Now again, this is where I say the Fed would lose the, you know, I think the Congress would rise up, the executive would use everything in their power to get their way.
turns.zh: 当然，这就是为什么我说美联储会输掉这一局——你知道，我认为国会会跳起来，行政部门会动用他们手中的一切力量来如愿以偿。

turns.en: But the point is, is the Fed, the reason the Fed has a pretty good track record in head to head competitions with the Treasury, and the reason the Fed is so powerful is because it is the banking arm and it is in many ways, not only the banking arm, but the distribution arm of the dollar system to the rest of the world.
turns.zh: 但重点是，美联储之所以在与财政部的正面较量中有相当不错的战绩、之所以如此强大，是因为它是银行体系的手臂，而且在很多方面，它不只是银行手臂，还是美元体系向世界其余地方分发的分发手臂。

turns.en: One of the arguments I make in the paper is that for this is what be, even though this is one of the reasons that the Fed has had this leverage over the Treasury for many, many years, there is a new capability or a new technology that's come about in the last five or 10 years that starts to put this back in the hands of the Treasury.
turns.zh: 我在报告里提出的论点之一是：对 Bessent 来说，尽管这正是美联储多年来一直对财政部握有筹码的原因之一，但过去五到十年间出现了一种新能力、或者说新技术，开始把这个筹码重新交回到财政部手里。

turns.en: And that is stablecoins. Stablecoins do not need a banking system to distribute either the bonds or to raise cash or to make payments. And so, as that technology gets built out, it starts to remove some of the leverage that the Fed has.
turns.zh: 那就是稳定币（stablecoins）。稳定币不需要一个银行体系来分发债券、来筹集现金、或者来完成支付。所以，随着这项技术被搭建起来，它开始削弱美联储所拥有的一部分筹码。

turns.en: And so, but the point is, is that as of right now, the Fed needs the Treasury and the Treasury needs the Fed. But we think that they are going to be more mutually working together, either by hook or by crook.
turns.zh: 所以，重点是，就目前而言，美联储需要财政部，财政部也需要美联储。但我们认为，他们将会更加相互协作，不择手段地走到一起。

turns.en: And having the ability at some point in the future to re-monetize the gold certificates, I think is a key factor in that. Now, I want to say, I am not expecting this anytime soon.
turns.zh: 而在未来某个时点拥有把黄金证书重新货币化（re-monetize）的能力，我认为这是其中一个关键因素。现在我想说的是，我并不预期这会在短期内发生。

turns.en: I don't think the government wants to do this. I don't think that's why Judy Shelton was brought on as a Treasury advisor. But I do think that they know that that's a possibility, and if and when that possibility or that insurance policy is needed, they want the ability to do it and do it quickly.
turns.zh: 我不认为政府想这么做。我不认为这就是他们请 Judy Shelton 来当财政部顾问的原因。但我确实认为，他们知道那是一个可能性，而一旦那种可能性、那份保单被需要时，他们希望有能力去做、而且能迅速去做。

turns.en: Well, let me take that crazy idea to an even crazier and more outlandish idea. What if you took the success of stablecoins and the trend Michael Everry has described around stablecoin statecraft becoming more and more embraced by the Trump administration as a tool of foreign policy?
turns.zh: 好吧，让我把这个疯狂的想法带到一个更疯狂、更异想天开的想法上。如果你把稳定币的成功，和 Michael Everry 所描述的、围绕“稳定币治国术”（stablecoin statecraft）正被 Trump 政府越来越多地当作外交政策工具来拥抱的这一趋势结合起来呢？

turns.en: And what if you said, look, we've got an even more grandiose idea than what you just described. Let's take all of the U.S. gold, 8,000 tons or whatever it is that they have in Fort Knox and other places.
turns.zh: 如果你说，看，我们有个比你刚描述的还要宏大的主意。我们把美国所有的黄金——不管他们在 Fort Knox 和其他地方存了8000吨还是多少——

turns.en: Let's take all of that gold and let's create a gold-backed stablecoin instead of just the existing U.S. dollar stablecoins that are tied to U.S. Treasuries.
turns.zh: 我们把所有这些黄金拿出来，创造一种黄金支持的稳定币，而不只是现有的、与美国国债挂钩的美元稳定币。

turns.en: We'll create a new one that's backed by gold and what we'll end up with is this gigantic stablecoin balance in the government's account, which represents all of those gold stablecoins.
turns.zh: 我们会创造一种由黄金背书的新稳定币，最终我们将在政府账户里得到这一笔巨大的稳定币余额，它代表着所有那些黄金稳定币。

turns.en: And now they can use them for any purpose they want in foreign negotiations, in foreign policy and so forth. I think there's a lot of risk and danger in that.
turns.zh: 然后他们就能把这笔钱用于对外谈判、外交政策等等任何他们想用的目的。我觉得这里面有很多风险和危险。

turns.en: I would not support it myself, but if you want to go to the next level, it seems like that's it. Well, so I think this is the point that I make.
turns.zh: 我个人不会支持它，但如果你想再上一个台阶，那看起来就是这个了。嗯，所以我觉得这就是我要讲的点。

turns.en: I don't expect that to happen, Eric, but I do think that you cannot rule it out, right? And I think from the government's perspective, listen, I think a lot of people think that the people that work at the Treasury in the Fed are a bunch of idiots.
turns.zh: 我不认为这会发生，Eric，但我确实认为你不能把它排除掉，对吧？而且我觉得从政府的角度看，听着，我想很多人以为在财政部和美联储工作的人都是一群蠢货。

turns.en: And I've often said they may be misaligned, they may be off base, they may be misguided, but these are not stupid people, especially the people at the top.
turns.zh: 而我常说，他们也许定位错了、也许判断失误、也许被误导了，但这些人不是蠢人，尤其是高层那些人。

turns.en: And so I think they know how they could use these different tools and they want to have these kind of tools in their toolbox if and when it comes.
turns.zh: 所以我认为他们知道该如何使用这些不同的工具，他们希望把这些工具放进自己的工具箱里，以备不时之需。

turns.en: So while I'm not expecting it, I think they want to have that ability. And then the other thing I would say, if you want to take it even further than what you took at Eric, is we're talking about right now about 8,000 tons of gold that the United States could do this with.
turns.zh: 所以尽管我并不预期它发生，我认为他们希望拥有那种能力。然后我想说的另一点是——如果你想比 Eric 你刚才推的再往前推一步——我们现在谈的是美国大约8000吨黄金，可以拿来做这件事。

turns.en: It just so happens, there's another 6,000 tons of gold sitting in the New York Fed that doesn't currently belong to the United States. But I would have a hard time seeing the United States sending that back to everybody if everybody requested it.
turns.zh: 而碰巧，纽约联储里还坐着另外6000吨黄金，目前并不属于美国。但我很难想象，如果大家都来要，美国会把那些黄金如数奉还给所有人。

turns.en: It wouldn't surprise me at all if they put a little notice on the door that said, we have now taken custody of this gold as our own for services previously rendered.
turns.zh: 如果他们在门上贴一张小告示，说“我们现已把这批黄金据为己有，作为对以往所提供服务的抵偿”，我一点都不会意外。

turns.en: And we've credited you with tokens in your account. So don't worry. And we have credited you. Exactly. This is my point. And so I often hear when we're getting towards these kind of in-game scenarios that there's only so much they can do.
turns.zh: “而且我们已经在你的账户里给你贷记了代币，所以别担心，我们已经给你记上了。”没错。这正是我的意思。所以当我们渐渐走向这类终局情形时，我常常听到有人说，他们能做的也就这么多了。

turns.en: The Fed is out of bullets. I've been doing this for 26 years now and for 25 of the 26 years, I've been hearing that the Fed is out of bullets.
turns.zh: 美联储没子弹了。我做这行已经26年了，其中25年里我一直听人说美联储没子弹了。

turns.en: And my point to people is that they have a lot more bullets than you can possibly imagine. And I think we're a long way from this type of thing happening.
turns.zh: 而我想告诉大家的是，他们的子弹比你所能想象的要多得多。而且我认为，离这种事情真正发生还远得很。

turns.en: It doesn't mean you shouldn't think about it. It doesn't mean you shouldn't be ready for it. But it also doesn't mean that you should wake up tomorrow and think this is going to happen.
turns.zh: 这不意味着你不该去思考它，不意味着你不该为它做好准备。但也不意味着你明天一醒来就该觉得这事要发生了。

turns.en: Okay. I want to go back to the basic premise here. So let's take the simple case of just revalue the gold that the government has 8,000 tons.
turns.zh: 好。我想回到这里的基本前提。所以我们先取那个简单的情形，就是把政府手里那8000吨黄金重新估值。

turns.en: You take it from $42 to $4,100, whatever it's trading out on the day. You say we're going to market and that means that you're going to suddenly have this gigantic increase in the Treasury general account.
turns.zh: 你把它从42美元提到4100美元，或者当天它交易到的任何价位。你说我们要按市价来，那意味着你财政部一般账户里会突然多出这么一大笔巨额增加。

turns.en: Okay. Well, you didn't really raise any capital. You just marked an asset to market. So what does this mean? Does it mean that the federal debt and debt to GDP ratio had actually been understated before and we're just correcting it to reality?
turns.zh: 好。可你其实并没有筹到任何资本，你只是把一项资产按市价重估了。那这意味着什么？意味着联邦债务和债务对GDP的比率之前其实被低估了，我们现在只是把它修正到真实水平吗？

turns.en: I mean, it seems like we're playing an accounting trick here. What's the other side of it? It is an accounting trick and it provides the government a bunch of money that they didn't have anymore than that money can get put into the economy and now there's more money in the some money supply.
turns.zh: 我是说，看起来我们在这儿玩的是一个会计把戏。那它的另一面是什么？它确实是个会计把戏，而且它给政府提供了一大笔它原本没有的钱，这笔钱一旦能被投入经济，那么货币供应量里就多了钱。

turns.en: And so each individual dollar in the money supply has now been reduced in value, right? And so this is an accounting trick. This is essentially what they did back in the, you know, the 20s of the 30s when they confiscated gold and then revalued it higher.
turns.zh: 于是货币供应中的每一美元现在的价值都被稀释了，对吧？所以这是个会计把戏。这本质上就是他们在上世纪二三十年代做过的事——当时他们没收了黄金，然后把它按更高的价值重估。

turns.en: It's just doing it again, but the numbers are a little bit bigger at this time. But the one thing I would say is that I don't think that they're going to do this yet because I don't think they need to do this yet.
turns.zh: 这不过是再做一遍，只是这次的数字更大一些。但我要说的一点是，我不认为他们现在就会这么做，因为我不认为他们现在就需要这么做。

turns.en: Again, we talked, we started this episode off about talking about how the dollar has gone up much to everybody's surprise. In my mind, the only time they would use gold would be if they had to bring back some kind of a bid to the dollar in order to bring the confidence back to it.
turns.zh: 再说一遍，我们这期节目开头就谈到，美元是如何在所有人都始料未及的情况下涨上来的。在我看来，他们唯一会动用黄金的时候，是他们不得不为美元重新找回某种买盘、以便把对它的信心带回来的时候。

turns.en: The fact that the dollar is going higher kind of shows that they don't really have to do anything for it to be in demand, right? And so, again, I think that it's important for the Fed and the Treasury to understand how this is a possibility.
turns.zh: 而美元正在走高这一事实，恰恰说明他们其实什么都不用做，美元就有需求，对吧？所以，我再一次认为，让美联储和财政部明白这是一种可能性，是很重要的。

turns.en: I think in many ways they own gold for the same reason probably that you and I and many others do is a form of insurance. And if the day ever comes, they want to be able to have it and be able to use it.
turns.zh: 我觉得在很多方面，他们持有黄金的原因，大概和你、我以及很多其他人一样，是把它当作一种保险。而如果那一天真的到来，他们希望能拥有它、并能用它。

turns.en: But I don't think that Scott Besant goes to bed at night saying, you know what, I cannot wait for January 1st because we're going to launch this gold stablecoin and remonetize gold.
turns.zh: 但我不认为 Scott Bessent 晚上睡觉时会想“你知道吗，我迫不及待等到1月1日了，因为我们要推出这个黄金稳定币、把黄金重新货币化”。

turns.en: I think that's pretty far down their list of ideas. Let's move on to US rates and what's going on with US rates and where they're headed. Something I've been quite interested in, you know, a lot of people are saying, oh boy, here we go.
turns.zh: 我觉得那在他们的点子清单上排得相当靠后。我们来聊聊美国利率吧，聊聊利率现在怎么回事、要往哪儿去。这是我一直很感兴趣的一个话题，你知道，很多人在说“哎呀，来了来了”。

turns.en: Rates are backing up. It means inflation is about to run away. And then I've talked to a couple of pretty credible people, including Harley Bassman saying, look, the data just don't show that this is an inflation problem.
turns.zh: 利率在往上顶，这意味着通胀就要失控了。可我又跟几个相当可信的人聊过，包括 Harley Bassman，他们说，看，数据根本显示不出这是个通胀问题。

turns.en: That's not what's driving it. And I'm kind of stuck with it. Really? Okay. What is driving it? I think it's a number of things. I think number one, I think, you know, there is some uncertainty with Trump's policies and what's going on in the world.
turns.zh: 推动它的并不是通胀。而我算是被卡在这儿了。真的吗？好。那到底是什么在推动它？我觉得是很多因素。第一，我认为，你知道，Trump 的政策和世界上正在发生的事确实带来了一些不确定性。

turns.en: I think people are perhaps not quite as excited to run out and buy a treasury as they used to be. Now, not being excited to run out and buy a treasury is not the same thing as wholesale rejection of the treasury.
turns.zh: 我觉得人们对冲出去买国债也许不像以前那么热衷了。不过，不那么热衷去买国债，和彻底摒弃国债，并不是一回事。

turns.en: So I want to be clear about that. But I think the fact that they're not as excited to buy them as they otherwise would be is part of the reason rates are going higher.
turns.zh: 所以我想把这点讲清楚。但我认为，他们不像本来那样热衷去买国债，正是利率走高的部分原因。

turns.en: One of the other things that I think reason that rates are going higher is it has to do with the AI trade that we were talking about. You know, I think to a certain extent, the AI trade is making the idea that maybe we're going to have some growth, maybe this new technology is going to provide some kind of a step function change and is going to allow us to kick the can down the road with all this debt or even potentially grow out of the debt.
turns.zh: 我觉得利率走高的另一个原因，跟我们谈到的 AI 交易有关。你知道，我认为在某种程度上，AI 交易正在让这样一种想法流行起来：也许我们会有一些增长，也许这项新技术会带来某种阶跃式变化（step function change），让我们能拖着这一大堆债务往后走，甚至有可能靠增长把债务消化掉。

turns.en: And as a result, you know, we want to get compensated more to a greater extent if we're going to buy government debt. And then there's a third thing that I think you'll understand what I'm saying.
turns.zh: 结果就是，如果我们要买政府债务，我们就会想在更大程度上拿到更多补偿。然后还有第三点，我想你会明白我在说什么。

turns.en: I don't know if you've thought of it in these ways, but I know you have spoken with Mike Green on several occasions. And I know you're probably familiar with his thesis on passive management.
turns.zh: 我不知道你有没有从这些角度想过，但我知道你跟 Mike Green 对谈过好几次，你大概也熟悉他关于被动管理（passive management）的论点。

turns.en: And in the same way that the effects of passive can drive stock prices higher just because there's a constant bid, that same thing can work on sovereign bonds when they start to get sold.
turns.zh: 而就像被动投资的效应能仅仅因为存在持续的买盘就把股价推高一样，同样的事情在主权债券开始被抛售时也会发生。

turns.en: And the passive effects that are working on the way up on stocks can work on the way down of an asset that is falling. And as interest rates go higher, bond prices fall and as bond prices fall, those bonds and those passive portfolios get sold.
turns.zh: 那种在股票上涨时起作用的被动效应，在一项资产下跌时也能反过来起作用。而随着利率走高，债券价格下跌，债券价格一跌，那些被动组合里的债券就被卖出。

turns.en: And it's not a human being sitting there making that decision. It's the machines that are making that decision. And as a result, you can get into some pretty severe dislocations pretty quickly as a result of the passive management in the same way that you can get into some dislocations pretty quickly on equity markets or risk assets due to passive management.
turns.zh: 而做这个决定的并不是坐在那儿的某个人，是机器在做这个决定。结果就是，你可能很快就陷入一些相当严重的错配（dislocation），就像被动管理能让股市或风险资产很快陷入错配一样。

turns.en: So I think there's a number of different things acting on it. It's not that I'm not concerned about the dollar or the rates going higher. I am concerned about rates going higher, but what really concerns me is the knock-on effects of U.S. rates going higher.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得有很多不同的因素在起作用。并不是说我不担心美元或利率走高。我确实担心利率走高，但真正让我担心的，是美国利率走高所带来的连锁反应。

turns.en: One of the analogies I've been using recently is the United States is still the big stack at the table. If you're thinking of a poker game, right, and this is a relative competition.
turns.zh: 我最近在用的一个类比是：美国仍然是牌桌上的大筹码（big stack）。如果你把它想成一场扑克牌局，对吧，这是一场相对的竞争。

turns.en: And if you're competing either for capital, you're competing on a military basis or you're competing on a geopolitical basis, the U.S. is still the big stack at the table.
turns.zh: 而无论你是在争夺资本、在军事层面竞争、还是在地缘政治层面竞争，美国仍然是牌桌上的大筹码。

turns.en: And when it's time to ante up or when the blinds come to you, if you're the big stack at the table, raising the blinds doesn't affect you as much as it does the smaller players at the table.
turns.zh: 而当轮到你下注、或者盲注轮到你时，如果你是桌上的大筹码，那么提高盲注对你的影响，就不如对桌上那些小玩家的影响大。

turns.en: And if you look at what's going on in rates in Europe and you look at rates in South America and you look at rates in some of the Asian countries, they're going up pretty severely too there as well.
turns.zh: 而如果你看看欧洲的利率、看看南美的利率、看看一些亚洲国家的利率，它们在那里也在相当剧烈地上行。

turns.en: And so one of the things I've encouraged people to think about is think about this as a game. And if you're the big stack at the table and you know that if you bet a big hand and maybe even you know that you're going to lose that hand, but if you also force another player to go into that hand and you force them to lose too, you start putting people out of the game and that kind of affects you.
turns.zh: 所以我一直鼓励人们去思考的一点是，把这个想成一场牌局。如果你是桌上的大筹码，你知道如果你押一手大牌、甚至你知道你可能会输掉那手牌，但如果你还能迫使另一个玩家也进那手牌、迫使他们也输，你就开始把别人赶出局，而那样反而对你有利。

turns.en: So what I mean by that is I have a slide in the slide deck that I gave you. It's slide 21 and it's basically saying, I'm showing a distribution curve, right?
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我给你的那套幻灯片里有一张，是第21张，它基本上是在说——我展示了一条分布曲线，对吧？

turns.en: And with the U.S. as the hegemon, there's a worst case scenario and there's a best case scenario. Now the best case scenario is it all just works out perfectly in your favor.
turns.zh: 而对于作为霸主（hegemon）的美国来说，有一个最坏情形，也有一个最好情形。最好情形就是，一切都完美地朝对你有利的方向发展。

turns.en: But there's a number of other potential outcomes and some of them mean you're going to take some risk and maybe even you're going to take some pain.
turns.zh: 但还有很多其他潜在的结果，其中一些意味着你要承担一些风险，甚至要承受一些痛苦。

turns.en: But as long as you take the far left tail off the table and you becoming the small stack is no longer an option, you don't really matter or you don't really mind too much if you get hit along the way as long as everybody else is getting hit more.
turns.zh: 但只要你能把最左边那条尾巴从桌面上拿掉、让“你变成小筹码”不再是一个选项，那么你就无所谓、或者说不太介意一路上挨几下，只要其他人挨得更狠。

turns.en: Now I'm not saying this is what they want, but my point is is the U.S. can accept a lot more pain than the rest of the world and still come out okay.
turns.zh: 我不是说这就是他们想要的，但我的意思是，美国能承受比世界其他地方多得多的痛苦，最后仍然安然无恙。

turns.en: And I think that's true whether we're talking about stock prices, whether we're talking about energy policy or whether we're talking about interest rates.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得，无论我们谈的是股价、是能源政策、还是利率，这一点都成立。

turns.en: And so the rates going higher in the U.S. are certainly a big deal. But I think when you zoom out and look at the whole forest and you see that the whole forest is on fire, the big picture starts to come more into focus.
turns.zh: 所以美国利率走高当然是件大事。但我认为，当你退后一步、看清整片森林、发现整片森林都在着火时，这幅大图景就开始变得更清晰了。

turns.en: You know, as I move on to the next slide, page 22 in the deck, this one really speaks to me and I should first disclaim that I am anything but an expert on fixed income and particularly carry trades.
turns.zh: 你知道，当我翻到下一张幻灯片——deck 里的第22页——这一张真的说到我心坎里了，我应该先声明，我绝不是什么固定收益专家，尤其不是套息交易（carry trade）专家。

turns.en: But I think back to the yen carry trade era that was just such a huge piece of finance. You had to take capital that mostly started in U.S. dollars and then you're going to short the yen and you're going to, I don't know, buy the New Zealand treasury or something and take advantage of this big differential and boy, there's a lot of moving parts in that.
turns.zh: 但我回想起日元套息交易那个时代，那曾是金融里如此巨大的一块。你得拿一笔大多以美元起步的资本，然后你要做空日元，你要去——我不知道——买新西兰国债之类的东西，来利用这个巨大的利差，天呐，这里面的活动部件可多了。

turns.en: As I look at this chart on page 22, I just say, wait a minute, isn't there a really ripe carry trade that's long U.S. treasuries and short Canadian treasuries right over the border, very liquid market, easy to access?
turns.zh: 当我看第22页这张图时，我就说，等等，是不是有一笔非常成熟的套息交易——做多美国国债、做空就在隔壁、市场非常流动、很容易参与的加拿大国债？

turns.en: And I think this chart right here was the foundation of my initial milkshake theory. Was that, yeah, rates per problem, we've been in an era where rates were going down for 40 years, right?
turns.zh: 而我觉得这张图正是我最初那个奶昔理论的基础。是这样吗，是的，利率这块的问题，我们一直处在一个利率下行了40年的时代，对吧？

turns.en: Nobody had ever really lost bonds and money and bonds in a big way. But then I thought in the years ahead, rates were going to go higher and while they would go higher in the U.S., they were going to go a lot higher for the rest of the world as well and it would hit them harder than it's hitting the United States, and so to your point, I think the trade you're suggesting is not a horrible one, right?
turns.zh: 从来没人真的在债券上、在货币和债券上大亏过。但后来我判断，未来几年利率会走高，虽然它们在美国会走高，但在世界其他地方会走高得多，对它们的冲击会比对美国的冲击更重。所以就你的观点而言，我觉得你建议的这笔交易并不差，对吧？

turns.en: I would much rather own U.S. dollars than own Canadian dollars or if you're a Canadian, you just buy dollars and then you buy a U.S.T. bill and as the Canadian dollar weakens versus the dollar, you make money there, but you also get an extra percent on the yields that you're earning in dollars and that's a way that the United States sucks in capital from around the world.
turns.zh: 我宁愿持有美元也不愿持有加元，或者如果你是加拿大人，你就买美元、然后买美国国库券，随着加元对美元走弱，你在那儿赚到钱，但你还在你赚取的美元收益率上多拿一个百分点，而这正是美国从全世界把资本吸进来的方式。

turns.en: I want to move on to another point you've made recently in some of your writings in social media, which is you've described a couple of things.
turns.zh: 我想转到你最近在你的一些文章和社交媒体上提出的另一个观点，你描述了几件事。

turns.en: One is the U.S. moving from a republic to an empire and you've also said that the current period in history is similar in many ways to the beginning of the Cold War as opposed to other times that people are tying it to.
turns.zh: 一是美国正从一个共和国（republic）走向一个帝国（empire），你还说，当前这个历史时期在很多方面更像冷战的开端，而不是人们常拿来类比的其他时代。

turns.en: What do you mean by those things? Well, when we came out of World War II, we obviously had a lot of debt from financing World War II and so we have a lot of debt now as well, right?
turns.zh: 你这么说是什么意思？是这样，当我们走出二战时，我们显然因为给二战融资而背上了大量债务，所以我们现在也有大量债务，对吧？

turns.en: And when we were leaving the late 40s or into the early 50s, we were embarking on this great Cold War with Russia. And I kind of feel like that's what we're embarking on now.
turns.zh: 而当我们在40年代末、进入50年代初离开那段时期时，我们正着手与俄罗斯展开这场伟大的冷战。而我有点觉得，那正是我们现在着手要做的事。

turns.en: We're embarking on this great Cold War with China now. I don't really want a Cold War with China, but I would prefer a Cold War to a Hot War.
turns.zh: 我们现在正着手与中国展开这场伟大的冷战。我其实并不想和中国打冷战，但比起热战，我宁愿要冷战。

turns.en: But regardless of which one we're in, I don't see it coming to an end anytime soon. And so I think the late 40s into the 50s is the better analog for what we're going through now than the 70s.
turns.zh: 但无论我们处在哪一种里，我都看不到它会在短期内结束。所以我认为，40年代末进入50年代，比70年代更适合拿来类比我们正在经历的事。

turns.en: I know there's a lot of people who think we're going to have this hugely inflationary time going ahead and as a result, the 1970s is the best analog.
turns.zh: 我知道有很多人认为我们前方会有一段极度通胀的时期，因此1970年代是最好的类比。

turns.en: But I actually think coming out of World War II is the better one. And the other thing that you mentioned as far as Republic to Empire, this is what I think many people miss.
turns.zh: 但我其实认为走出二战那段是更好的类比。而你提到的另一点，从共和国到帝国，这正是我觉得很多人所忽略的。

turns.en: I think it's very easy to look at the United States and you look at the different problems that we have and listen, they are innumerable. But if you look at the problems the United States has right now and you look at the problems that Rome had, let's say between 120 and 60 BC, they are extremely similar.
turns.zh: 我觉得，看美国、看我们有的各种不同问题很容易——听着，它们多得数不清。但如果你看看美国现在有的问题，再看看罗马比如公元前120年到公元前60年之间有的问题，它们极其相似。

turns.en: You had a number of foreign wars that were draining the Treasury. You had inequality in the citizens. Certain citizens had the right to vote and others didn't.
turns.zh: 你有一堆在耗尽国库的对外战争。你公民之间存在不平等。某些公民有投票权，另一些没有。

turns.en: You had cult of personalities. You had political infighting. And so the similarities are very, very similar. And when people make those comparisons of Rome to the United States, then the natural answer is, well, Rome fell, so then the United States is going to fall.
turns.zh: 你有个人崇拜。你有政治内斗。所以这些相似之处非常非常像。而当人们拿罗马和美国做这种类比时，那么自然的答案就是，嗯，罗马垮了，所以美国也会垮。

turns.en: But they miss perhaps the most important chapter in that whole story. And that is that what came after the fall of the Roman Republic was the Roman Empire.
turns.zh: 但他们也许错过了这整个故事里最重要的那一章。那就是，在罗马共和国（Roman Republic）垮台之后到来的，是罗马帝国（Roman Empire）。

turns.en: And the reason is because a strong man wrote in and said, we're not going to have this nonsense anymore. We're not going to be politically disunified.
turns.zh: 而原因在于，一个强人骑马而来，说，我们不再搞这些乌烟瘴气的东西了。我们不会再政治上四分五裂。

turns.en: We are not going to have multiple different priorities. We are going to consolidate power and we are going to remain Rome and we are going to continue to run the Mediterranean, if not the world.
turns.zh: 我们不会再有各种不同的优先事项。我们要把权力集中起来，我们要让罗马延续下去，我们要继续统治地中海、乃至整个世界。

turns.en: And I think that is the more likely scenario for the United States now than one where the United States falls and becomes a second class citizen on the global stage.
turns.zh: 而我觉得，比起美国垮台、沦为全球舞台上的二等公民那种情形，这才是当下美国更可能出现的情形。

turns.en: Now, again, this doesn't bring me great pleasure in saying this. I certainly hope there's a way that this doesn't become the case. But if I have to choose between that chapter coming next and failure, I think this is the more likely chapter to come next.
turns.zh: 当然，说这些并不让我感到愉快。我当然希望有办法让事情不至于如此。但如果我必须在“接下来是那一章”和“失败”之间做选择，我认为“接下来是那一章”的可能性更大。

turns.en: And so I think the combination of all the debt in the world which causes all these problems, the fact that we have this Cold War kind of breaking out with China, the fact that we have a very powerful republic that in many ways has seen its institutions fall, that leads me to think more about a Republican Rome than it does the fall of the Soviet Union if we're going to make an analogy for the United States.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，世界上所有那些债务引发所有这些问题这一事实、我们与中国之间正在爆发的这场冷战这一事实、我们有一个在很多方面已目睹其制度崩塌的强大共和国这一事实——所有这些都让我在拿美国做类比时，更多想到共和制的罗马，而不是苏联的解体。

turns.en: Let's move on to the Cold War analogy. I agree very strongly with the Cold War analogy. I'm just not always certain, is it U.S.-China or is it U.S. against a formative bloc that's China and Russia and not sure fill in the blank?
turns.zh: 我们来聊聊这个冷战类比。我非常强烈地认同冷战这个类比。我只是不总是确定，它是美中之间，还是美国对抗一个由中国和俄罗斯组成、还不确定、你来填空的阵营？

turns.en: Who are we beginning a Cold War with? Well, I think it's primarily with China. But I think that great power competition with China is going to force countries or regions or factions to take sides.
turns.zh: 我们是在和谁开始一场冷战？嗯，我觉得主要是和中国。但我认为，与中国的这场大国竞争，将会迫使各国、各地区或各派系选边站。

turns.en: I don't think many countries are going to be able to just sit on the sidelines. I think they are going to be forced to choose one side or the other.
turns.zh: 我不认为很多国家能就那么袖手旁观。我觉得他们会被迫选择站在这一边或那一边。

turns.en: And so whether it ends up just being with China or whether it ends up being with a bloc, I guess I'm not quite smart enough to know. But I think regardless of which one it is, I think this probably plays out for a number of years if not a number of decades.
turns.zh: 所以无论最终只是和中国，还是和一个阵营，我想我没聪明到能知道答案。但我认为，无论是哪一种，这大概都会持续好些年、甚至好几十年。

turns.en: I don't see this all like coming to a head in the next six to nine months and then we're on to the next thing. I think the pendulum of history was swinging towards globalization for 30 or 40 years.
turns.zh: 我不认为这一切会在未来六到九个月里就摊牌、然后我们就转向下一件事。我认为历史的钟摆曾朝全球化方向摆了三四十年。

turns.en: And now I think that pendulum of history is going to swing back the other way for 30 or 40 years. And as part of this, what you mentioned earlier about the AI, the rise of AI, I think that's a huge part of the Cold War.
turns.zh: 而现在我认为，历史的钟摆将朝另一个方向摆回三四十年。而作为其中一部分，你早先提到的 AI、AI 的崛起，我认为那是冷战中很大的一块。

turns.en: And I think it will be very difficult to win the overall power competition if you don't win the AI race as well. And so I think these two are very much intertwined.
turns.zh: 而且我认为，如果你赢不了 AI 竞赛，就很难赢下这场整体的权力竞争。所以我觉得这两者是紧密交织在一起的。

turns.en: Brent, I couldn't agree more and I want to go a little deeper on that topic of AI and the Cold War because I was really taken aback when Matt Berry told our listeners on this program that he sees something on the horizon, which is look, the Chinese models, the Chinese open source AI models that you can get for free if you are willing to run them on your own hardware.
turns.zh: Brent，我再同意不过了，我想在 AI 和冷战这个话题上再深入一点，因为当 Matt Berry 在我们节目里告诉听众他看到地平线上有个东西时，我真的很吃惊，那就是——看，中国模型、中国的开源 AI 模型，只要你愿意在自己的硬件上运行，你就能免费拿到。

turns.en: They're only three to six months behind the frontier labs models. This is not chat GPT-3 anymore, where the thing just barely does what you need.
turns.zh: 它们只落后前沿实验室（frontier labs）模型三到六个月。这已经不是 ChatGPT-3 那种、东西勉强能干你要的活的年代了。

turns.en: For almost all users of AI, except for the people that are solving unsolvable math problems, you don't need Fable 5.1. Opus is plenty strong enough.
turns.zh: 对几乎所有 AI 用户来说，除了那些在解无解数学难题的人，你并不需要 Fable 5.1。Opus 就足够强了。

turns.en: And it says to me that it's not going to be very long before open source free AI from China. Maybe it's not as good as the US frontier models are, but it's still good enough that it can solve most corporate problems.
turns.zh: 这在我看来意味着，用不了多久，来自中国的开源免费 AI——也许不如美国的前沿模型那么好，但仍然好到足以解决大多数企业问题。

turns.en: And the point that Matt Berry made is the real game changer here could be that it doesn't just work as good as AI used to three months ago from the frontier labs, but it also solves your problem with the frontier labs mining your data because if you're forced to run it on your own hardware, you can air gap it so that anthropic and open AI never get the ability to have your corporate decision-making data pass through their cloud.
turns.zh: 而 Matt Berry 提出的点是，这里真正的游戏规则改变者可能在于，它不只是能和三个月前前沿实验室的 AI 一样好用，它还解决了前沿实验室挖你数据的问题，因为如果你被迫在自己的硬件上运行它，你就能把它做物理隔离（air gap），让 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 永远没机会让你的企业决策数据从他们的云上过一遍。

turns.en: Matt's saying that could potentially be a huge upset where everybody, including US corporations, says, yes, AI is totally the future, but just like other stuff where we buy cheap stuff from China where it's cheaper, we can get cheap or free open source models from China and we don't need open AI or anthropic anymore, that would crash the private credit market that's formed behind AI, that the consequences of that would be horrendous.
turns.zh: Matt 说的是，这可能是一场巨大的颠覆：所有人，包括美国企业，都会说，是的，AI 绝对是未来，但就像我们从中国买便宜货一样，哪儿便宜买哪儿，我们可以从中国拿到便宜或免费的开源模型，我们不再需要 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 了——那将会让围绕 AI 形成的私人信贷市场崩盘，其后果将是灾难性的。

turns.en: What do you think about that theory? I have to say that it's definitely a concern and I don't know that I agree with 100%, but I certainly don't disagree with it 100%.
turns.zh: 你怎么看这个理论？我得说，这确实是个令人担忧的事，我不确定我百分之百同意，但我当然也没有百分之百不同意。

turns.en: And I think this is probably a good opportunity for me to say this because I think perhaps sometimes when people hear me talk, they misunderstand my position on China.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得这也许是我该说这句话的好机会，因为我想有时候人们听我讲的时候，会误解我对中国的立场。

turns.en: I think China is an extremely formidable adversary. I do not think that it is just an automatic given that the United States wins this power competition.
turns.zh: 我认为中国是一个极其强劲的对手。我不认为美国赢下这场权力竞争是理所当然、自动就成立的事。

turns.en: I think that this is a huge competition with, and I think China needs to be taken very seriously, the fact that their electricity output in some ways gives them a fantastic leg up in this race, especially if they can use that electricity, the ability to run their AI industry on that electricity, and even if they don't necessarily are leading the frontier, if they're just either right there or right behind it, does it really matter?
turns.zh: 我认为这是一场巨大的竞争，我认为必须非常严肃地对待中国——他们的电力产出在某些方面给了他们在这场竞赛中一个极好的先机，尤其是如果他们能用这些电力来驱动他们的 AI 产业的话；而且即便他们未必在引领前沿，只要他们就在那儿、或者就紧跟其后，那真的要紧吗？

turns.en: And so I have to, before I forget, somewhat related to this, one of the best podcasts I have heard all year was your conversation with Carly Anderson.
turns.zh: 所以在我忘记之前，跟这个多少有点相关，我今年听过的最好的播客之一，就是你和 Carly Anderson 的那场对谈。

turns.en: I had never heard of her before, but I'm going to pay attention to her now because I think what she was saying and the stuff that she's working on sits right at the heart of this great battle.
turns.zh: 我之前从没听说过她，但我现在会开始关注她了，因为我认为她所说的话、以及她在做的那些东西，正好处在这场大战的核心。

turns.en: And if the United States is able to figure out a way to create some energy sources that allows them to continue leading the AI race and it allows them to stay ahead of China, then I think the US has a chance.
turns.zh: 而如果美国能想办法创造出某种能源来源，让他们得以继续引领 AI 竞赛、让他们能保持在中国之前，那么我觉得美国就有机会。

turns.en: If they are not able to do that, and if China continues to nip at the heels and do it in a much cheaper way than the United States has so far, I think it's not a given by any means, and I think it's an open game.
turns.zh: 如果他们做不到，而如果中国继续紧咬不放、并且用一种远比美国迄今便宜得多的方式来做，我认为这绝非板上钉钉，我觉得这是一场开放的对局。

turns.en: And so that's why I've, but this then also bleeds into other things. This is part of the reason why chips are being weaponized. It's part of the reason that traditional energy is being weaponized.
turns.zh: 所以这就是为什么我——但这也渗透到其他事情里。这是芯片被武器化的部分原因。这是传统能源被武器化的部分原因。

turns.en: It's part of the reason that Marco Rubio was in Iceland a few days ago. It's part of the reason that we went into Venezuela earlier this year.
turns.zh: 这是 Marco Rubio 几天前出现在冰岛的部分原因。这是我们今年早些时候进入委内瑞拉的部分原因。

turns.en: All of this stuff in my mind is just a derivative of this great power competition. And so for much of the first 20 years of my career, the landscape was kind of set and it was known, even though there was volatility in financial markets, the geopolitical situation was relatively calm and somewhat known.
turns.zh: 在我看来，所有这些东西都只是这场大国竞争的一个衍生结果。所以在我职业生涯头二十年里的大部分时间，格局是相对固定、也是已知的，尽管金融市场有波动，地缘政治局势却相对平静、也算已知。

turns.en: But now not only do we have volatility in financial markets, but we have volatility in social aspects of the world. We have volatility in the way maps are drawn and the geopolitical aspects of that.
turns.zh: 但现在，我们不仅金融市场有波动，我们在世界的社会层面也有波动。我们在地图如何绘制、以及由此而来的地缘政治层面有波动。

turns.en: We have volatility in the energy markets, which is needed to run every other market. This kind of goes back to my initial premise of the show, and I said, I think all of these challenges is what's going to lead to the United States Treasury and the United States Fed needing to come together in order to win this great power competition.
turns.zh: 我们在能源市场有波动，而能源是运转其他每一个市场所必需的。这多少回到了我这期节目开头的那个前提，我说过，我认为所有这些挑战，正是将会导致美国财政部和美联储需要走到一起、以赢下这场大国竞争的东西。

turns.en: Because by no means do I think it's a given. Well, first of all, thank you for the kind words about the Carly Anderson interview. Believe it or not, I was a little disappointed in myself for that interview because Carly is freakishly smart.
turns.zh: 因为这绝不是一件板上钉钉的事。嗯，首先，谢谢你对我提到 Carly Anderson 那场访谈的美言。信不信由你，我对那场访谈其实对自己有点失望，因为 Carly 聪明得离谱。

turns.en: That interview scraped maybe 2% off the top of how much is in her head. And I look forward to getting her back on. We'll have to see what the listener reaction is on that one.
turns.zh: 那场访谈顶多刮下了她脑子里所装东西的2%。我期待能把她再请回来。我们得看看听众对那期的反应如何。

turns.en: We're trying to make macro voices as listener-driven as possible. So if you want us to bring back more Carly Anderson or do an unplugged session with her, let us know.
turns.zh: 我们在努力把 MacroVoices 做得尽可能由听众驱动。所以如果你想让我们多请几次 Carly Anderson、或者跟她做一期不加剪辑的深聊专场，告诉我们。

turns.en: Make some noise on Twitter and we'll respond accordingly. Please make an exception for her. Well, you know what we just... That's a really good idea because what we just did, we conceived it for Anasal Haji and we just did it for Michael Everry is we keep the feature interview at 45 to 55 minutes because that's kind of our target and it works well for our people whose time is very valuable and they can't afford more.
turns.zh: 在 Twitter 上闹出点动静，我们会相应回应。“请一定为她破个例。”嗯，你知道吗，我们刚刚……这是个好主意，因为我们刚做的那件事——我们是为 Anasal Haji 设计的、又刚为 Michael Everry 做了一遍——就是把重点访谈控制在45到55分钟，因为那大致是我们的目标，也很适合那些时间非常宝贵、腾不出更多时间的人。

turns.en: But then we did a bonus hour afterwards to go deeper. And I mean, if I did that with Carly, we'd need a bonus weekend in order to get into what's in that woman's brain.
turns.zh: 但之后我们做了额外一小时的加更来深入探讨。我是说，如果我跟 Carly 这么干，我们得加更一整个周末，才能触及那个女人脑子里装的东西。

turns.en: Anyway, let's come back to the rest of this. China and energy, you're just talking about current electricity, at least as I thought I understood you.
turns.zh: 总之，我们回到剩下的话题。中国和能源，你谈的只是当前的电力，至少我以为我是这么理解你的。

turns.en: China's got more nuclear power plants, conventional nuclear power plants, planned and under construction than the entire US fleet. They've got an energy strategy that includes a whole bunch of advanced research on thorium-fueled molten salt reactors, which are something that really nobody in the private sector except for a couple of companies that are struggling to succeed have even dared to take on.
turns.zh: 中国在建和规划中的核电站、传统核电站，比美国整个核电站机队还多。他们有一套能源战略，包含大量关于钍基熔盐堆（thorium-fueled molten salt reactors）的前沿研究，而这东西私营部门里几乎没人敢碰，除了几家正挣扎求存的公司在做。

turns.en: And the couple of guys that are trying to do it, I mean, they're fighting against a state-funded competitor, which is China. So if you're really, I'm afraid that you're right, that the assumption that, oh, if it's a cold war with China, we're going to win because rah, rah, rah, you and I are both born in the United States.
turns.zh: 而那几家想做的家伙，我是说，他们是在和一个国家出资的对手较量，也就是中国。所以如果你真的……恐怕你是对的，那种“哦，如果是和中国打冷战，我们赢定了，因为万岁万岁，你和我都生在美国”的假设——

turns.en: So that's what we should think. Gosh, the facts and evidence are pretty daunting. I want to hit a final topic before we close because we are coming up on that normal interview length deadline, which is AI and the perception of so many people in today's society that well, AI is going to take our jobs, they're going to completely destroy the economy.
turns.zh: 所以那才是我们该想的。天呐，事实和证据相当令人望而生畏。我想在收尾前谈最后一个话题，因为我们快到那个正常的访谈时长上限了，那就是 AI，以及当今社会里这么多人的一种看法：嗯，AI 会抢走我们的工作，会彻底摧毁经济。

turns.en: I think in the long term that is ludicrous, that's like saying that the invention of tractors is going to destroy farming. Well, it's the biggest productivity tool ever.
turns.zh: 我认为从长期看这是荒唐的，那就像说拖拉机的发明会摧毁农业一样。喂，它可是有史以来最大的生产力工具。

turns.en: And if you look at what tractors did for farming, I'm going to argue that AI is the white collar equivalent of that, that will make all white collar workers a hundred times more productive than they ever could have imagined before, except there's one thing.
turns.zh: 而如果你看看拖拉机为农业做了什么，我要说，AI 就是它的白领版本，会让所有白领工作者的生产力达到他们以前想都不敢想的一百倍，只不过有一件事。

turns.en: That's the long term. If you're the guy, if you're one of the thousand field workers that got replaced by the one farmer that was driving the tractor in your immediate timeframe, yeah, it did take everybody's jobs.
turns.zh: 那是长期而言。如果你就是那个人，如果你是那被一个开着拖拉机的农民取代掉的一千名田间工人之一，那么在你眼前的这段时间里，是的，它确实抢走了所有人的工作。

turns.en: Longer term, those people got new jobs, they learned how to drive tractors, but they were kind of screwed for a while and it resulted in a lot of political turmoil and frankly, geopolitical and local political unrest.
turns.zh: 更长期看，那些人找到了新工作，他们学会了开拖拉机，但他们在一段时间里挺惨的，而且这导致了很多政治动荡，坦白说，还有地缘政治和地方上的政治不安。

turns.en: Where are we headed with this whole AI taking everybody's jobs thing? I am not one of these apocalyptic, you know, we got to shut all the AI down because it's going to kill us people.
turns.zh: 那么，这场“AI 抢走所有人工作”的事情，我们要走向何方？我可不是那种末日论者、那种“我们得把所有 AI 都关掉，因为它要杀了我们”的人。

turns.en: I actually think it is going to be a step change function for the better of humanity. That's in my base case, I recognize the dangers and I'm not saying that we should not be concerned at all, but I actually think in the overall art, it is going to be a positive.
turns.zh: 我其实认为它将会是一次让人类变得更好的阶跃式变化。这是我的基准情形，我承认其中有危险，我不是说我们完全不该担忧，但我确实认为从整体上看，它将会是一件正面的事。

turns.en: And to your point, I don't think it is necessarily going to be something that leads to the downfall of economic output. And in many ways, I think it could be fantastic.
turns.zh: 而且就你的观点而言，我不认为它一定会导致经济产出的崩塌。在很多方面，我觉得它可能棒极了。

turns.en: What I think it is, I think there will be short term problems with unemployment. My guess is the way that this is going to be handled and I'm going to put a caveat here that I should have said at the very beginning is that when I talk about this stuff, I do my best not to talk about what I would like to see happen because what I would like to see happen in many ways doesn't matter.
turns.zh: 我认为它会带来的，是短期里的失业问题。我猜它被处理的方式——我在这儿要加个限定词，其实一开始就该加——就是当我谈这些东西时，我尽量不去谈我希望发生什么，因为我希望发生什么在很多方面并不重要。

turns.en: I typically try to talk about what I think is going to happen, whether I want it to or not. And that's definitely the case with this next comment that I think one of the ways this will probably be at least try to be addressed is some form of universal basic income or even further expansion of the welfare state, which again, this is not a prescription.
turns.zh: 我通常尽量去谈我认为将会发生什么，无论我想不想它发生。而我接下来这句评论就绝对是这样：我认为其中一个大概会被用来应对的方式，是某种形式的全民基本收入（universal basic income），甚至是对福利国家的进一步扩张——再说一遍，这不是一剂处方。

turns.en: This is not my recommendation, but I think that is probably the most likely outcome because the last thing you want is a bunch of unemployed, upset people with no money with nothing better than to do than go out into the streets and protest.
turns.zh: 这不是我的建议，但我认为那大概是最可能出现的结果，因为最糟糕的就是有一大群失业、愤怒、身无分文的人，除了上街抗议没有更好的事可做。

turns.en: So I think as we look forward 10, 20, 30 years, it's probably going to be a fantastic thing, the AI. But I think it could be a pretty bumpy road until we get to that escape velocity.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，往前看10年、20年、30年，AI 大概会是件了不起的事。但我认为，在我们达到那个逃逸速度（escape velocity）之前，可能会是一段相当颠簸的路。

turns.en: On that note, Brent, I can't thank you enough for another terrific interview. But before I let you go, tell our listeners a little bit more about what you do at Santiago Capital.
turns.zh: 就说到这里，Brent，我再感谢不过了，又是一场精彩的访谈。但在放你走之前，跟我们的听众多讲讲你在 Santiago Capital 做的事吧。

turns.en: If they want to get the full version of your latest missive, which again is called disparate, not desperate, but disparate housewives referring to the marriage between the Fed and Treasury.
turns.zh: 如果他们想拿到你最新那篇文章的完整版——再强调一次，它叫 disparate，不是 desperate，是《Disparate Housewives》，指的是美联储和财政部之间的那场“联姻”。

turns.en: How do they find out more about what you do? Yeah. Well, so the first place to go is to SantiagoCapital.com. Long story short, we are a registered investment advisor.
turns.zh: 他们要怎么进一步了解你做的事？好的。嗯，第一个要去的地方是 SantiagoCapital.com。长话短说，我们是一家注册投资顾问（registered investment advisor）。

turns.en: We provide holistic financial structuring and implementation of portfolios for high net worth individuals and families. As part of that, we also manage a private fund.
turns.zh: 我们为高净值个人和家庭提供整体性的财务规划以及组合的落地实施。作为其中一部分，我们还管理一只私募基金。

turns.en: And then finally, from the research side of things, if you go to research.santiagocapital.com, you'll see our different research offerings. That's where you'll be able to access the report that we've been talking about today.
turns.zh: 然后，从研究这一侧来说，如果你去 research.santiagocapital.com，你会看到我们不同的研究产品。那就是你能拿到我们今天一直在谈的这份报告的地方。

turns.en: And what we do there is we try to talk about big kind of think pieces that we think are going to impact the markets and perhaps the world in the months and years ahead.
turns.zh: 而我们在那里做的，是尽量去谈一些大的思考性文章（think pieces），我们认为它们会在未来几个月和几年里影响市场、乃至影响世界。

turns.en: And then we will typically also talk about how we think that impacts portfolios as far as things to be concerned about, things to be looking out for, and things to position for.
turns.zh: 然后我们通常还会谈到，我们认为这会如何影响投资组合——哪些是该担忧的、哪些是该留意的、哪些是该提前布局的。

turns.en: So, and then finally, you know, I'm pretty active on social media. Twitter is always one of my favorite places to blow off some steam and have a little fun.
turns.zh: 所以，最后，你知道，我在社交媒体上挺活跃的。Twitter 一直是我最喜欢的、发泄一下、找点乐子的地方之一。

turns.en: So if any of those different platforms is a way to interact with us, and I appreciate you having me back on, I always enjoy speaking with you.
turns.zh: 所以如果这些不同的平台里有任何一个是与我们互动的方式——我很感激你能再请我来，我一直很享受和你交流。

turns.en: And again, folks, that's SantiagoCapital.com. Now it's time for our Macrovoices Market Desk segment. Patrick, where's the trade? Thanks, Eric.
turns.zh: 再说一次，各位，就是 SantiagoCapital.com。现在是我们 MacroVoices Market Desk 环节的时间了。Patrick，交易机会在哪儿？谢谢，Eric。

turns.en: Brent's central argument is that the U.S. dollar can continue attracting capital even as higher rates create stress because the pressure falls harder on more vulnerable economies.
turns.zh: Brent 的核心论点是，即便更高的利率制造了压力，美元仍能继续吸引资本，因为压力会更重地落在那些更脆弱的经济体身上。

turns.en: He specifically highlighted his preference for the U.S. dollar over the Canadian dollar for this week's trade. We're expressing that view through options on the Canadian dollar futures.
turns.zh: 他特别强调了他对本周交易的看法：做多美元、做空加元。我们通过加元期货上的期权来表达这个观点。

turns.en: What attracts me is the pricing. Implied volatility remains below 5%. Now we've seen cheaper levels, but that still looks reasonable for currency that has recently moved 260 pips, roughly 3.5% from peak to trough in just 27 days.
turns.zh: 吸引我的是定价。隐含波动率（implied volatility）仍低于5%。虽然我们见过更便宜的水平，但对于一种最近27天里就从峰到谷波动了260点（pips）、大约3.5%的货币来说，这看起来仍然合理。

turns.en: The market is moving, yet the premium required to express a directional view remains modest. So here's the structure. With the Canadian dollar trading around 70.37 U.S. cents, I'm looking at buying the 70-cent put option expiring on November 6, 2026 with about 29 days remaining.
turns.zh: 市场在动，然而表达一个方向性观点所需的溢价仍然温和。所以结构是这样的：在加元交易于约70.37美分附近时，我在考虑买入行权价70美分、2026年11月6日到期、还剩约29天的看跌期权（put option）。

turns.en: It is quoted at 22 pips, the equivalent of about 220 U.S. dollars per standard contract before costs. That gives us short Canadian dollar exposure with positive gamma and vega while limiting the options risk to the premium.
turns.zh: 它报价22点，在扣除成本前相当于每张标准合约约220美元。这给了我们做空加元的敞口，同时带有正的 gamma 和 vega，并把期权风险限定在权利金之内。

turns.en: The Brent allows for a near-term U.S. dollar pullback, so the Canadian dollar rebound is a real possibility. The put defines our exposure to that adverse move while preserving participation if the Canadian dollar weakness resumes.
turns.zh: 而 Brent 认为美元近期会回调，所以加元反弹是一种真实的可能。这张看跌期权界定了我们对那种不利走势的敞口，同时在加元重新走弱时保留了参与度。

turns.en: For perspective, a return to 69 cents would represent a 137-pip decline from our reference price. At expiration, the put would have 100 pips of intrinsic value after deducting the 22-pip premium.
turns.zh: 换个角度看，如果回到69美分，将意味着相对我们的参考价格下跌137点。到期时，在扣除22点权利金后，这张看跌期权会有100点的内在价值。

turns.en: That leaves 78 pips of profit, approximately three and a half times the amount risked. Now the trade does require timely downside follow-through.
turns.zh: 那就留下78点的利润，大约是所冒风险的三倍半。当然，这笔交易确实需要及时的向下跟进。

turns.en: If the underlying futures finish above 70 cents, the premium is lost. A sharper decline or volatility expansion could also provide an opportunity to monetize before expiration.
turns.zh: 如果标的期货收在70美分以上，权利金就损失掉了。而更剧烈的下跌或波动率放大，也可能提供一个在到期前变现的机会。

turns.en: Given that premium, I prefer the defined risk and convexity of the put to an outright future short position. It's a modest premium commitment to express Brent's dollar thesis through the currency already capable of a meaningful short-term move.
turns.zh: 考虑到那笔权利金，比起直接做空期货，我更喜欢看跌期权那种有界的风险和凸性（convexity）。这是一笔不大的权利金投入，用来通过一种本就有能力出现有意义短期波动的货币，来表达 Brent 的美元论点。

turns.en: That's where's the trade. Patrick analyzes and trades the markets every day over at Big Picture Trading. Macrovoices listeners can sign up for a free two-week trial at bigpicturetrading.com.
turns.zh: 这就是“交易机会在哪儿”。Patrick 每天都在 Big Picture Trading 分析和交易市场。MacroVoices 的听众可以在 bigpicturetrading.com 注册免费试用两周。

turns.en: Now back to Patrick and Maseel. All right Patrick, let's talk about the 10-year treasury yield now hitting 5.35% in the 30-year and our climbing to almost 5.8.
turns.zh: 现在把时间交回给 Patrick 和 Michelle。好的 Patrick，我们来谈谈10年期美债收益率现在触及5.35%、30年期也攀升到接近5.8的事。

turns.en: But equities continue to hold near their highs. Now these markets seem to be telling a very different story depending on where you're looking.
turns.zh: 但股市继续守在接近高位的地方。这些市场似乎在讲着非常不同的故事，取决于你往哪儿看。

turns.en: But what could stabilize bonds and how much longer can stocks withstand this pressure? This story on yields continues to be the core thesis.
turns.zh: 但什么能让债市企稳，股市又能顶住这种压力多久？关于收益率的这条故事线仍然是核心论点。

turns.en: We continue to see an incredibly strong bond sell-off, continued pressure on yields. This has certainly caused the hurdle rate for valuations to hurt so many of the financial assets out there.
turns.zh: 我们持续看到一场极其强烈的债券抛售、收益率持续承压。这当然已经让估值所用的门槛利率（hurdle rate）伤害到了市面上如此之多的金融资产。

turns.en: We have clearly two different regime expectations. Equities continue to hold up in suggesting that they think that the earnings growth can absorb this higher borrowing cost, but the bonds repricing continue to show substantial pressures that eventually could force repricing of equity prices.
turns.zh: 我们显然有两种不同的机制预期。股市继续撑住，暗示它们认为盈利增长能够吸收这更高的借贷成本，但债券的重新定价持续显示出巨大的压力，最终可能迫使股价重新定价。

turns.en: This pressure is definitely visible beneath the surface. We continue to see horrible market breadth where earlier in the week we were at 20% of stocks above their 50-day moving averages, which is basically 4 out of 5 stocks are clearly correcting and only a few of these equity names continue to hold up.
turns.zh: 这种压力在表面之下绝对可见。我们持续看到糟糕透顶的市场广度（market breadth）：本周早些时候，站上50日均线的股票只有20%，基本上就是五只股票里有四只在明显回调，只有少数几个股票名称还在撑住。

turns.en: Now on the very short term, we've seen some relief on the SOFR futures bouncing a little bit as there's a little bit less hawkish near-term policy outlook on there.
turns.zh: 而在极短期内，我们看到 SOFR 期货上有一些缓解、小幅反弹，因为近端政策展望没那么鹰派了。

turns.en: Oil could change all of this if we saw another meaningful rise and inflation expectations continue to be the story. We could see the short-term interest rate markets re-resume their prevailing downtrends.
turns.zh: 油价可能改变这一切，如果我们看到它再度有意义地上涨、而通胀预期继续是那条主线的话。我们可能会看到短期利率市场重新恢复它们原有的下行趋势。

turns.en: There's a lot of stress in the bond markets. The big question, of course, is if and when this will translate to some potential reactions in the equity markets.
turns.zh: 债市里有很大压力。当然，最大的问题是，这何时、以及是否会传导到股市里、引发一些潜在的反应。

turns.en: All right. Now that brings us to equities, Patrick. The S&P 500 is broken out to new highs and the NASDAQ remains pretty strong, but participation beneath the surface is still pretty thin.
turns.zh: 好。这就把我们带到股市了，Patrick。标普500（S&P 500）已突破到新高，纳斯达克（NASDAQ）也相当强劲，但表面之下的参与度仍然很薄。

turns.en: Do you think this increasingly small group of leaders, you know the MAG-7s and all the tech semiconductor names, keep the rally going? Or do you think this bond market pressure is bringing us closer to a broader correction?
turns.zh: 你觉得这个越来越小的领涨群体——你知道的，七巨头（Mag 7）和所有那些科技、半导体名称——能把涨势延续下去吗？还是你觉得这种债市压力正把我们带向一次更广泛的回调？

turns.en: It's funny you referenced the MAG-7 because increasingly it's becoming a MAG-2. Really the majority of these hyperscalers have actually been stuck in a range and it's only Nvidia and Microsoft that continue to press higher.
turns.zh: 有意思的是你提到了七巨头，因为它正越来越变成一个“二巨头”（Mag 2）。实际上，这些超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）中的大多数一直卡在一个区间里，只有 Nvidia 和 Microsoft 在继续往上顶。

turns.en: Like I was saying earlier, the breadth of the market continues to be under a huge stress. The big question, of course, is which one will prevail?
turns.zh: 就像我刚才说的，市场广度持续承受着巨大压力。当然，最大的问题是，哪一方会占上风？

turns.en: Could we see some breakthrough in what's happening in the Middle East and a de-escalation that drops inflation pressures and suddenly alleviates all of these stresses on the equity markets and allows a meaningful rebound in so many of these beaten down names?
turns.zh: 我们会不会看到中东局势出现某种突破、出现降级，从而压低通胀压力、突然缓解股市上的所有这些张力，让这么多被砸下去的名称出现一次有意义的反弹？

turns.en: Or will we finally see that this very thin leadership finally succumbs to the selling? This is important to note because we are seeing some systematic triggers sitting down around the 7700 level on the S&P, about 2.5% off the recent highs.
turns.zh: 还是我们终将看到，这个非常薄的领涨群体最终屈服于抛售？这一点很重要，因为我们看到标普在7700那个位置附近坐着一些系统性触发点（systematic trigger），大约离近期高点2.5%。

turns.en: This is important because there's a lot of these systematic trading strategies that have been structurally long in this market and certainly some estimates are there as much as $85 billion on a down market to sell.
turns.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为有很多这类系统性交易策略一直在这个市场里结构性做多，而且当然有一些估计认为，一旦市场下行，有多达850亿美元要卖出。

turns.en: The question becomes, do one of these MAG-7s, let's say Nvidia began a market correction on the short term, could that be all that the S&P needed in order to hit one of these triggers and begin selling?
turns.zh: 问题就变成，如果这些七巨头里的某一个——比如 Nvidia——在短期内开始一轮市场回调，那会不会就正好是标普所需要、去触及其中一个触发点并开始卖出的那根导火索？

turns.en: Right now, the story has 100% been that the market cap weighted index continues to hold along its highs, but again, when you look at the Russell and you look at just the equal weight S&P 500, both of them are decisively in a downtrend.
turns.zh: 眼下，故事百分之百都是市值加权指数继续守在它的高位附近，但同样，当你看 Russell、看单纯的等权重标普500时，它们两个都果断地处在下行趋势里。

turns.en: Something's got to give and the only way I see the S&P 500 actually breaking higher is if there was relief in the rates markets that allow many of these beaten down stocks to come up for a breath.
